title: Regional fill patterns hypothesis — weekly notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick weekly capture of an experiment-oriented hypothesis: regional fill patterns (how traffic surfaces into regional edge pools) are creating predictable troughs we can pre-fill with opportunistic low-priority jobs to reduce cold-starts and improve SLA headroom.

Snapshot / TL;DR:
- Observation window: 2026-09-25 -> 2026-09-30 (5 working days) across eu-west1, us-west2-edge, apac-sg
- Measured: sustained 99th p95 token latency increase during local-night windows for eu-west1 (01:30-03:30 UTC) and apac-sg (15:00-17:00 UTC) correlated with windowed backfill eviction events.
- Hypothesis: small, repeatable troughs (~10-15% spare capacity) appear at predictable daily offsets; opportunistic prefill (low-priority priming jobs) can flatten troughs and reduce 95th latency regressions by ~6–9% without increasing committed spend.

Observations (raw notes):
- eu-west1: average fleet utilization 78% daytime -> dips to 63% at troughs; troughs last ~80–140m depending on region; backfill churn increases by 2.3x during trough start.
- us-west2-edge: frequent short spikes (12–20s) immediately after trough exit that cause KV cache miss storms for large-context sessions.
- apac-sg: trough alignment shifted by ~45m vs forecast; likely because consumer fraction from regional partners has shifted with new partner rollout.
- Prewarming experiments (small sample) reduced first-token latency by 18% for n=120 sessions but increased aggregate token throughput by <0.5% (good).

Data and instrumentation gaps: (things to collect next week)
- Need per-queue eviction timestamps (currently only aggregated per-host).
- Missing time-aligned KV cache-hit rate series for long-context sessions (>2k tokens).
- Need to add a short-lived probe that simulates 3x session replays at trough start to measure cache regen behavior.

Hypotheses (detailed):
1) Predictable troughs exist because customer workloads have regionally aligned night/off-peak schedules; these troughs are large enough (10–20% capacity) to host prefill without impacting committed workloads.
2) Opportunistic prefill with low-QOS jobs that maintain KV warm state reduces p95 latencies during next peak window via cache hit propagation; benefit depends on session mix (chat vs long-completion).
3) Trough misalignment (apac shift) is caused by new partner traffic that didn't include timezone metadata in their provisioning flow — we can correct routing rules to improve alignment.

Experiment proposals (next 2 sprints):
- Pilot A (eu-west1): schedule 6 x 10–15m low-priority priming bursts starting 45m into known trough, run for 10 business days. Measure p95 latency pre/post next-day peak, KV hit rate, and eviction rates. Jira: INFRA-4317.
- Pilot B (us-west2-edge): synthetic probe at trough exit (simulate 50 sessions of 512 token warmups) to quantify spike-triggered cache miss storm severity. Low-risk; runs only on canary slice.
- Pilot C (apac-sg): coordinate with Partner Onboarding (SOX-ops) to add timezone metadata to their region tags and observe trough alignment over 7 days.

Risk matrix / guardrails:
- If priming increases sustained utilization >5% for committed instances during peak windows, pause and revert priming script.
- Don’t touch dedicated pools (reserved capacity). Priming limited to opportunistic/backfill nodes only.
- Rate-limit priming CTL to 2x current backfill concurrency to avoid eviction amplification.

Operational checklist (playbook sketch):
- Before run: snapshot regional utilization, current backfill occupancy, active preemptible window start times.
- During run: monitor p95/gross-latency, eviction rate, and prefill job churn logs. Auto-trigger stop if eviction rate up >15% vs baseline.
- After run: 48h post-run latency heatmap, memory residency delta, and sample KV longevity traces.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Add eviction timestamp metric to telemetry pipeline (Liam Ortega) — ETA 2026-10-07.
- Implement canary priming controller script with rate-limiter (Ethan Zhao) — ETA 2026-10-09.
- Coordinate partner tagging change (Sofia Martinez) — ETA 2026-10-12.
- Quick dashboard card for trough detection (mini-alert) (Priya Nair) — ETA 2026-10-08.

Open questions / discussion points for infra triage:
- Should priming jobs be weighted by model family (large-context models benefit more) or simple uniform probes? Pros/cons in cost/benefit.
- What's the safest default QOS setting for priming to minimize disruption while maximizing KV residency?
- Is there value in extending this to Dedicated pools where customers allow prewarming (opt-in)? Legal/compliance + cost implications.

Meeting notes (2026-10-02 weekly sync):
- Quick sync with SRE and Serving Runtime: consensus to run Pilot A canary on 10% of opportunistic capacity.
- Serving runtime flagged need for kernel-warm metrics so we can see model-level cold path triggers. Action: runtime team to add kernel-warm counter (Francis PR queued).
- Finance: asked for estimated spend delta; agreed pilots should be neutral to committed spend and billed to experiment budget.

Next steps for next weekly capture:
- Start Pilot A canary (eu-west1) and surface first 48h telemetry.
- Get eviction timestamps online and validate probe runs.
- Revisit detection thresholds; align on auto-stop for priming.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep naming consistent: call priming "op-fill" in configs to avoid mixing with prewarming dedicated.
- Chat with Product (hosted-api) next Monday to see if they want opt-in endpoint-level prewarm flag for heavy customers.

Appendix (quick numbers snapshot):
- Sample region eu-west1 trough depth: 15% avg spare on 2026-09-29 01:45 UTC 
- p95 latency delta at trough exit: +320ms -> normalized to baseline 1.18x 
- Backfill eviction count spike: +47% at trough transitions
